country: United Kingdom, Spain, Italy, France, Germany

links.outcome: Proportion of notes with at least one Critical+High documentation error, AI vs clinician notes
links.effect: AI notes had fewer Critical+High errors: 24.4% vs 61.0% (calibrated reviewer; RR 2.50) and 6.2% vs 21.8% (clinician adjudication; RR 3.50). Nonzero AI error burden remained; difference largest for omissions.
links.quote: On the principal safety outcome — the paired probability that a note carried ≥1 Critical+High error — clinician notes were affected more often under both detection arms: 61.0% versus 24.4% by the calibrated reviewer (relative risk 2.50, 95% CI 2.09–3.00) and 21.8% versus 6.2% by clinician adjudication (relative risk 3.50, 95% CI 2.32–5.27).

links.outcome: Fraction of documentation errors identified by unaided clinician review versus calibrated automated reviewer
links.effect: Unaided clinician review identified roughly 12% of the errors the calibrated reviewer retained, and a smaller fraction in AI notes than in clinician notes.
links.quote: Unaided clinician review identified roughly 12% of the errors the calibrated reviewer retained, and a smaller fraction in AI notes than in clinician notes.

links.outcome: AI scribe note quality (PDQI-9) versus clinician notes by site/language
links.effect: AI notes scored higher than clinician notes in all five sites and languages (dz 0.41–0.75); overall 40.6 vs 35.6, difference +5.08.
links.quote: AI notes scored higher than clinician notes on the PDQI-9 (40.6 vs 35.6; difference +5.08, 95% CI 4.6–5.6; Cohen’s dz=0.55), consistently across all five sites (dz 0.41–0.75), and were less dispersed (5.7% of AI vs 27.8% of clinician notes fell below the study pre-specified low-score threshold (<32)).

unlisted_practices: Using a calibrated automated LLM reviewer to detect documentation errors, validated against a clinician panel
Paired comparison of AI-scribe notes against clinician-written notes on the same consultations

screen.reason: Evaluates the documentation quality, safety, and error rates of an ambient AI scribe against clinician-written notes in a multi-country simulation study.
